items.followUp: If 12 cm³ of ethanol is used to prepare 150 cm³ of aqueous solution, calculate its percentage concentration by volume.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the solute and solution volumes.
rubric.description: Identifies the given volumes, with correct SI conversions.
rubric.how: Look for 5 cm³ of acetone and 90 cm³ of solution, or their equivalent SI volumes.

rubric.why: Award for selecting the volume-per-volume percentage formula.
rubric.description: States the correct formula for percentage concentration by volume.
rubric.how: Look for volume of solute divided by volume of solution, multiplied by 100.

rubric.why: Award for substituting the given SI volumes correctly into the formula.
rubric.description: Substitutes the SI volumes into the formula.

rubric.why: Award for the correctly calculated concentration.
rubric.description: Gives the percentage concentration by volume.

modelAnswer: Given: Volume of acetone = 5 cm³ = 5 × 10⁻⁶ m³; volume of solution = 90 cm³ = 9 × 10⁻⁵ m³.
Formula: Percentage concentration by volume = (volume of solute ÷ volume of solution) × 100.
Answer: The aqueous solution has a concentration of 5.56% (v/v).

items.followUp: Define one atomic mass unit and give its value in grams.

rubric.why: Award for defining the atomic mass unit using the carbon-12 reference.
rubric.description: Defines one atomic mass unit as one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
rubric.how: Look for one-twelfth (1/12) and a reference to carbon-12.

rubric.why: Award for the correct approximate value in grams.
rubric.description: Gives the value of one atomic mass unit in grams.

modelAnswer: One atomic mass unit (u) is 1/12 (one-twelfth) of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of sulfur (S₁₆) in subshells.

rubric.why: Award for correctly filling the first ten electrons into subshells.
rubric.description: Writes the first three occupied subshells correctly.

rubric.why: Award for correctly placing the remaining seven electrons.
rubric.description: Completes the chlorine subshell configuration correctly.
rubric.how: Look for 3s² 3p⁵, giving 17 electrons in total.

modelAnswer: Its electronic configuration in subshells is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵.

items.followUp: Why does atomic size generally increase from top to bottom in a group?

rubric.why: Award for identifying the increase in nuclear charge across a period.
rubric.description: States that the number of protons and nuclear charge increase from left to right.
rubric.how: Look for increasing proton number or nuclear charge.

rubric.why: Award for explaining why increased nuclear charge reduces atomic size.
rubric.description: Links added electrons in the same shell and stronger nuclear attraction to a smaller atom.
rubric.how: Look for electrons entering the same shell and being pulled closer to the nucleus.

modelAnswer: Across a period, the number of protons increases, so the nuclear charge increases.
The added electrons enter the same principal shell, so shielding does not increase much; the stronger attraction pulls the electrons closer to the nucleus and decreases atomic size.

items.followUp: Why does atomic size increase from top to bottom in a group?

rubric.why: Award for explaining that the outermost electron is farther from the nucleus down a group.
rubric.description: Links the increase in electron shells to the greater distance of the outermost electron from the nucleus.
rubric.how: Look for more shells and the outermost electron being farther from the nucleus.

rubric.why: Award for connecting shielding and weaker attraction to the decrease in ionization energy.
rubric.description: Explains that increased shielding reduces attraction, so less energy is needed to remove an electron.
rubric.how: Look for increased shielding, weaker nuclear attraction, and less energy required to remove the outermost electron.

modelAnswer: Down a group, the number of electron shells increases, so the outermost electron is farther from the nucleus.
Increased shielding weakens the nucleus’s attraction to the outermost electron, so less energy is needed to remove it; therefore, ionization energy decreases.
